item.title: The U Street Corridor: Past Glory, Present-Day Questions
item.description: Black Neighbors of 1617 U Street, formed by residents in 2023, is pushing for affordable housing in the U Street NW neighborhood, which has seen gentrification and displacement of long-term residents, while also advocating for the Green New Deal for Housing Act to preserve affordable housing via social housing. The post The U Street Corridor: Past Glory, Present-Day Questions appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Emmet Cohen and Janelle Gill Named DCJF 2026 Artists-in-Residence
item.description: The DC Jazz Festival has named Emmet Cohen and Janelle Gill as its 2026 Artists-in-Residence who will host a year of performances, master classes, and creative collaborations throughout the city to celebrate jazz as a vibrant, evolving art form. The post Emmet Cohen and Janelle Gill Named DCJF 2026 Artists-in-Residence appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Angola and the Atlantic Bridge: A New Chapter for African-American Partnership
item.description: Angola is emerging as a strategic and economic partner for the United States, with major infrastructure initiatives and a focus on renewable energy, making it a key destination for American businesses and investors. The post Angola and the Atlantic Bridge: A New Chapter for African-American Partnership appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Washington Gas Celebrates Black History Month
item.description: Washington Gas is celebrating Black History Month by profiling one of its employees, Bryan Lipscomb, who is a Senior End User Computing Specialist and carries forward the legacy of service, leadership, and commitment to making a meaningful difference in the communities he serves. The post Washington Gas Celebrates Black History Month appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DANIELS: ‘All Boots on the Bridge’ State of Emergency Without Urgency in Black America
item.description: The National Urban League's State of Black America Report has warned of a state of emergency in Black America due to the MAGA movement's assault on democracy, civil rights, and progress, and has called for an urgent, collective, visible, public response by Black organizations and leaders to create the psychological momentum to spark a massive response by Black people to the danger to democracy and the danger to Black America. item.title: Civil Rights Leaders Demand End to $2.13 Tipped Wage, Call It a Legacy of Slavery
item.description: Justice, political and labor leaders gathered in New York to call for the passage of Living Wage for All legislation, which would raise the minimum wage to $30 an hour in New York and $25 an hour federally, and eliminate all subminimum wages, in order to address the racial and gender wage gaps exacerbated by the federal tipped wage of $2.13 an hour. The post Civil Rights Leaders Demand End to $2.13 Tipped Wage, Call It a Legacy of Slavery appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Snow, Wind and Cancellations Paralyze D.C. as Nor’easter Roars Up East Coast
item.description: Winter Storm Hernando brought heavy snow and powerful wind gusts to the mid-Atlantic, causing flight cancellations, rail service disruptions, and power outages for tens of thousands. The post Snow, Wind and Cancellations Paralyze D.C. as Nor’easter Roars Up East Coast appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Inside Out: A View of Hope from Incarceration
item.description: The Lorton Prison photography program, which ran from 1980 to 1989, offered incarcerated men a creative outlet to express themselves and connect to the outside world, and now their photos are being showcased in the exhibition "Inside Out: Dignity and the Art of Seeing" at the DC Commission on the Arts and Humanities. The post Inside Out: A View of Hope from Incarceration appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Milk & Honey Turns Dining Into Impact With Divine Nine Initiative
item.description: Thompson Restaurants' Milk & Honey brand is partnering with D.C.'s Divine Nine network to raise funds for scholarships and service efforts, with diners able to contribute by rounding up their checks and participating in the Black Love Dine & Donate Day. The post Milk & Honey Turns Dining Into Impact With Divine Nine Initiative appeared first on The Washington Informer.
